Pillage mode drastically changes the tactical aspect of the game.

1. Normally, your team and the enemy team take turns in a back-and-forth manner. You play a unit, they play a unit, you play a unit and so on. This is also true if – for example – the enemy has eight units and your team has three. This leads to situations where a player with two units can completely steamroll an enemy team of ten or more units, if they play their cards right.
2. In Pillage mode, the team with the most units gets to take the most turns. 

I'd recommend that you start playing the game unmodded, and if you feel like you're getting a hang of it, give the mod a try and see how it changes the game completely.

Hi <@776783603274481674> and welcome. 🙂 

When it comes to modding Banner Saga, you could say there are three levels of depth.

1. Firstly, you have save file editing. This requires nothing more than a text editor, but only modifies a limited set of stats from an existing save file. This includes what party members you have, what decisions you have made, morale, items, supplies and all that.
2. Then there's *.json* editing, which requires a specifically built decompiler program, which is easy to obtain. .json file editing is appropriate for modifying the stats regarding battles, events and characters' and items' inherent properties. 
3. Then there's *.air* editing, which I used to dabble in a lot, but in which I only ever managed to get a few small things to work. This is where the guts of the game lie, and where the central game mechanics are defined to then be balanced in .json. 

As for the chance to hit, I believe we're in level 3 territory, because it's not a central mechanic in Banner Saga by default. Off the top of my head, my only suggestion would be to take the miss chance properties of the *Last Stand* and *Gold-Tusk Boar* items (which only exist in BS3) and put them on all items in the game. Then there's the fact that until October of 2017, Oli used to have a bug where after using Axe Storm, he would have a miss chance on all attacks for the rest of the battle. If someone has an older version of Banner Saga 2, perhaps they could look into why that happened? Another suggestion would be to add a %dodge item (or talent, if that's possible?) to all enemies.

As for the number of days wounded, it's tied to the diffculty setting of the game, which gives me hope that it could be edited from the .json file, or level 2 as I've named it in this post. 

The WIL bonus from morale also sounds like level 3 stuff.

My thoughts on the platforms you can choose:

1. Forum-type posts (reddit, Steam) -- Would give your work more exposure, but may be a hassle responding to feedback or editing/correcting. Also, input is mostly limited to text and images, and markup and sectioning requires care.

2. GoogleDoc -- Probably the easiest, just throw in text, code, and figures/screenshots, make lists, search-and-replace, and what not. Other people can read and (if you want) comment too. You can also add trusted peolpe (like us lot 😛 ) as "editors". Sheets/Excel can also be used for "productivity", e.g., a ToDo list with progress, timestamp/version, notes, assignee etc.

3. GitHub -- The best for minimizing backend work, sharing the code, tracking errors etc. It will however restrict interaction to people who are accustomed to these tools (software development in general).
Or better yet, a git repo where you can track and document every line of code and hurl curses at when there is a merge conflict
